notes.title: Souls of the Silent Tide Update is Out Now for Everyone!
notes.content:
[p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44962233/b3d4c14f7fb85095f5292faa589ccd87259fdef4.png"][/img][/p][p]Greetings, ladies, gentlemen, and any eldritch entities watching us from the void!  We are proud to announce that the first major Content Update, [b]Souls of the Silent Tide, is now available[/b] for everyone to download! The game will also be [b]20% off for one entire week, starting at 7 PM CEST / 10 AM PT today[/b], which makes it the perfect time to grab it.[/p][previewyoutube="g5KIwzMS8jk;full"][/previewyoutube][p]This new update features the otherworldly House of Mists with its surrounding Blood Forest area, a ghastly ritual site of the head witch Agata, as well as a secret surprise for the most diligent and perseverant of explorers (an achievement is linked to this secret – let us know if you find it, but don’t spoil it for the others!). These locales will be brought to life with new intriguing characters and deadly enemies, together with new challenging puzzles and quests. The whole [b]Change Log[/b] can be found below.[/p][p][i]Stygian: Outer Gods [/i]has also been localized with subtitles for players across the globe. New languages now include: [b]French, German, Spanish, Brazilian Portuguese, Simplified Chinese, Russian and Japanese[/b].
[/p][p]We would like to thank everyone who helped with the beta testing, your feedback and suggestions were invaluable! We were able to fix a lot of bugs thanks to your reports and we are continuously monitoring what you have to say! Join our [u][url="https://discord.gg/cxVGx6K5ZT"]Discord[/url][/u] and share your opinion.[/p][p]It is necessary to mention that after the 20% discount ends on Friday 29th at 7 PM CEST, the price of Stygian: Outer Gods will change to 24,99 USD / EUR. This makes the discount even more of a bargain and this is definitely the best time to get yourself a copy of the game, if you haven't done so yet.[/p][p]To sweeten the deal, Stygian’s older brother, Stygian: Reign of the Old Ones, is [b]discounted by 80%[/b] all week long as well. If you haven’t played the first game, this is the perfect chance to check it out.

notes.title: Stygian: Outer Gods | Daniel Upton's Notes: Alternative Means of Combat
notes.content:
Greetings, ladies, gentlemen, and any eldritch entities watching us from the void!

What happened in Kingsport long ago crossed the threshold of ordinary fear; and few of those who survived ever spoke of it. But sometimes, a memento of that time appears - a torn scrap of paper, a mark on the wall, a few hastily carved words - a vessel for the voices of those who lived through the nightmare.

And those voices… They can teach us how to live through it too.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44962233/c0aefb25a2223ad22a70d04c7460c173f54c5b85.png[/img]

Kingsport isn’t just a regular place. It’s a nexus of reality and nightmare, a place where the hero comes face to face with the forbidden - with things no human was meant to witness. Here, you don't just fight monsters - every last moment you have to fight to stay sane, while reality unravels around you. In a world like this, you need every advantage you can get, as fights in Stygian: Outer Gods are brutal and unforgiving. That is why we want to talk about what makes the game's combat system stand out - and what many players tend to overlook or underestimate, to their detriment.

Don't expect to be given an arsenal of high-powered weapons. Even though as you progress through the game, you can find various firearms, at the start, you find a knife, a rusty sickle, maybe an axe; but what many fail to realize is that almost anything you can pick up can be used in combat, amplifying your strength and improving the odds of your survival. If you wish to succeed in your quest, you need to keep in mind that In Stygian, anything can become a weapon:
[list]
[*]  A crate on the street.
[*]  A bucket by the well.
[*]  A wooden chair in a forgotten room.
[*]  A glass bottle rolling across the pub floor.
[/list]
These aren’t just decorations; they become a lifeline in the most desperate of situations.

Picture it: you're wounded, bleeding, barely standing, and something terrible is closing in… You're out of bullets, and lack the strength to swing a blade anymore.
But then - your hand finds something, as you desperately scramble around - a bottle.
You barely have time to think, but some instinct buried deep down, the primal need for survival, takes over and you throw it. And while you await the inevitable as you hear the growls just a few feet away, a miracle happens; a glass shattering, and a whimper.

For one single second, the creature stumbles. And that precious second… That is all you need. To get up and flee. Or to compose yourself and finish the fight.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44962233/107da885ae9c201ff2c689d59247f8c7dc871591.gif[/img]

There are plenty of reasons to use this mechanic:
[list]
[*] To interrupt a charging enemy.
[*] To create an opening for your own attack.
[*] To start the fight with a surprise strike.
[*] To buy a precious moment and retreat.
[*] And of course, to distract an unaware enemy and sneak around them.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44962233/46a87f2a4f0ef1f2e196cdda83a601ae42c64e75.gif[/img]

We deliberately built a world where there is no perfect weapon that can win every fight. Everything depends on your situation - and on your ability to improvise.
You’re not an invincible action hero - you’re just someone trying to stay alive inside a nightmare.
Throwing objects isn’t a gimmick - it’s a tactical tool.

If you’ve never tried hurling something into the face of a nightmare… now’s the time. It’s more satisfying than you’d think. And can be more effective than you’d hope.

Thank you - for playing Stygian: Outer Gods. For venturing with us into this bleak, broken world. For daring to stare into the abyss… 
And perhaps you can already feel the abyss staring back.
Don't blink.

notes.title: Stygian: Outer Gods | The Performance Patch Goes Live for Everyone
notes.content:
Greetings, ladies, gentlemen, and any eldritch entities watching us from the void!

Our performance patch has just gone live for everyone after being thoroughly tested both internally by our team and with volunteers from our community through the public beta. We'd like to thank especially those of you who participated in the beta testing and helped us by sharing your own experience and feedback; we appreciate all your support so much!

The update's primary focus, as the name suggests, was [b]to improve the game's performance[/b], but it also added Victoria's voice to more dialogues and fixed the "Burglar in Training" achievement. Along with the patch, we've also enabled [b]cloud saves[/b], another feature you requested, and we've heeded your call! Performance remains our priority, and we will work on improving it throughout Early Access while also generally polishing the game based on your feedback and adding more content. 

However, expect incremental, gradual progress in this matter, not one single update that would completely revolutionize how the game runs on weaker machines. We also strongly recommend considering the minimum PC specs stated on the game's store page before buying Stygian: Outer Gods. Nevertheless, please keep sharing your feedback with us, especially regarding the performance.

To stay in touch and share your thoughts, please feel free to use the Steam discussions or [url=https://discord.gg/vd6eRT6weF]join the Stygian: Outer Gods official Discord[/url] where not only can you chat with other Stygian adorers, you can also share your ideas, fan-arts, music taste and climb the user ranks!

Thank you once again! If you're among those who "celebrate" Walpurgis Night today, on April 30, what better place to hunt witches than in Stygian's Kingsport, hmm?

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2581410/Stygian_Outer_Gods/

notes.title: Stygian: Outer Gods | Come Try the Performance Patch Now!
notes.content:
Greetings ladies, gentlemen, and any eldritch entities watching us from the void!

As the [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2581410/view/537725541533352173]prophecy foretold[/url], we are approaching the completion of our [b]performance patch[/b]. Alas, the Old Ones are unpredictable and their favor ever-fickle, therefore we are asking for volunteers to gaze upon our latest creation before we unleash it upon all our players!

We have been testing the update thoroughly ourselves, and we will keep doing so for several days more - yet there might be issues and bugs that have slipped through. That is why we are only allowing those who deliberately choose to enter to experience it for now; and if all goes according to plan, the update shall be released to everyone [b]next week[/b].

If you wish to heed this call, all you need to do is right-click on Stygian: Outer Gods in your Steam client Library and go to properties - betas, click on the drop-down menu next to "Beta Participation" and select "[i]public_beta[/i]":

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44962233/6360ba5a248058c18f74a2287933768d19bed4d9.png[/img]

Your game will then update to this experimental version - besides improved performance, you will also be able to hear Victoria's voice in more dialogues, and the achievement of "Burglar in Training" will be properly awarded as well. Anytime you wish to return to the public, stable version of the game, just follow the same steps and select "[i]None[/i]" from the beta list

Just don't forget, brethren - [b]help us[/b] by reporting any problems and issues you encounter on your journey to Kingsport and beyond. Most importantly, let us know whether you feel the performance improvements we strive for - and if you can, include your computer specifications and the settings you play at with your reports. Share your impressions here in the comments, in [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/2581410/discussions/0/604154444533259218/]Steam Discussions[/url] or, even better, come join our ranks on the official [url=https://discord.gg/AzSgYMkbfw]Stygian: Outer Gods Discord server[/url]!

Thank you, and may your descent into madness be swift and joyous!

notes.title: Stygian: Outer Gods | First Post-Launch Patch
notes.content:
Greetings ladies, gentlemen, and any eldritch entities watching us from the void!

We are excited to see how many of you have heard the call and rushed to the mists of Kingsport since we've launched Stygian: Outer Gods into Early Access yesterday! And we've already gleamed valuable insight from watching you play from afar as well as reading your posts and reviews and chatting with those of you who have joined our Discord server. And we have already prepared and just released a remedy for several problems plaguing your nightmares, both serious and small. 

The complete list of changes can be found below, but first, we would like to assure you that besides the removal of pesky bugs and addition of new areas, monsters, plot twists and mysteries into the game, improving its performance IS among our top priorities. We are already exploring several avenues of how to achieve this and make sure that your in-game experience is as smooth as possible. Alas, such is the nature of Early Access, that we needed to see how the game performs for more different settings on different machines than what we can ever hope to test ourselves, despite our best efforts. We therefore ask for a little more patience before you pass your judgment while we finish [b]a performance patch that we are working on.[/b]

You see, all your feedback is beneficial and helps us in our endeavor to unleash the Stygian nightmares upon the world; however, if you share what troubles you with us in the form of a negative review, even if it is well-intentioned, it both hurts the game as well as impedes our ability to ask follow-up questions and investigate the problems more dilligently. In short, it makes it more difficult for us to improve the game and rectify the bad impression it has left on you. Therefore we implore you, if you see potential in our project and would like to see it grow, and even shape the form it takes, instead of sharing your woes through a negative review, come join us either in the Steam Discussions, or talk to us and your brethren players on our official [url=https://discord.gg/AzSgYMkbfw]Discord server[/url] - we will be forever grateful.

And now, behold what we have prepared for you in this short span of time:

[list]
[*] Fix for the visual display of the injuries (pulsating icons).
[*] Fix of the disappearance of the boatman some people experienced.
[*] Fix of missing interaction after the release of the Shackled.
[*] Added "Speech" checks for quest with paintings, Bethan and the lighthouse keeper.
[*] The location of the kerosene lamp has been changed.
[*] Added visual effects for skill cards.
[*] The lockpicking check for the Safe Room door in the mines has been removed.
[*] Improved balancing of reactions and health for ghouls, making them more formidable.
[*] Added voiceover for Victoria, The Boatman and the Masked Servant.
[*] Various other minor fixes and changes.
[/list]

notes.title: Stygian: Outer Gods | The Story, the World and its Roots in the Franchise
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44962233/5ae1dd273dc835f08f7c524c472562b3bc7db284.png[/img]
Greetings ladies, gentlemen and any eldritch entities watching us from the void!

It’s been a while since we last shared any news following the announcement of Stygian: Outer Gods, and given the season of ever-lengthening darkness giving rise to the tendrils of madness and despair reaching out from the depths of night, gripping and squeezing our minds all day long… Erm, well. What we meant to say is, Happy Holidays everyone! We think it’s the right time now to lift the curtain a little and give you a first taste of what’s coming with Stygian: Outer Gods next year.

One of the most frequently asked questions since the announcement has been about the game’s connection to Stygian: Reign of the Old Ones. Yes, they are indeed connected; as we are developing a prequel set in the misty town of Kingsport, before the Black Day began. Arkham is still located in Massachusetts, and its residents are living their ordinary lives.

Creating a game within an already established universe while doing justice to the original source material - the works of H.P. Lovecraft - is both a great honor and a true challenge for us. Especially considering the transition from a side-view classic RPG to an immersive first-person experience in full 3D.

Our team approaches this with utmost care. We hope to not only delight the old guard of H.P. Lovecraft fans but also attract new ones, introducing them to his unique take on horror and the genre his mind gave birth to.

It’s important to note that while the game is a part of the Stygian universe, and we aim to connect our prequel’s story to the original Stygian: Reign of the Old Ones in many ways, we are very much making a standalone game, with its own unique features, accessible to complete newcomers to the franchise as well.

[h2]The World[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44962233/6a91ab1b8b3455edbcc2393035ee308c09137496.png[/img]

As we have already mentioned, the game takes place in the misty town of Kingsport, which plays a key role in the future fate of the world. Due to bloody, profane rituals conducted deep within a local mansion, this place has become a locus for Lovecraftian nightmares that lie in wait, ready to ensnare any and all unwelcome guests. Players will have the chance to visit iconic locations from many of H.P. Lovecraft’s works: a lighthouse of the old keeper, a mysterious mansion, an abandoned church, and others.

[h2]The Story[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44962233/32285b67063c4e41d5a0a0d5a53f644a8b8742df.png[/img]

The game’s narrative is deeply rooted in the Stygian universe, reflecting its themes and lore. To ensure authenticity and seamless connections, we consulted with the narrative designer of Stygian: Reign of the Old Ones. His insights helped us align the story, weaving it into the overarching universe and tying all elements together cohesively.

The game's protagonist is a former anthropologist and soldier, discharged due to a severe injury. Struggling with a fragile and deteriorating mental state, he is haunted by recurring nightmares and consumed with guilt over the unresolved disappearance of his father.

At the start of the game, everything shifts dramatically for our hero, and his life takes on a new purpose. He receives an invitation from a young woman to join an expedition to Kingsport, a secluded, enigmatic place that captivated his father’s interest. This journey offers not only a chance to uncover the secrets of Kingsport but perhaps also the key to understanding his father’s mysterious fate.

Players will find themselves drawn into a labyrinth of mysteries and hidden schemes, where every character harbors their own secret motives, shrouded in layers of deceit. As the clock ticks, the ominous arrival of the Black Day looms ever closer, leaving little time to unravel the truth. And as for the enigmatic Dismal Man—what role does he play in this unfolding drama? That’s a tale for another time, we will not be uncovering that particular secret today.

[h2]The Legacy[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44962233/a7758cdf1cae5cd821a6998ed6981c105c03080d.jpg[/img]

As they explore the town, players will encounter a variety of characters, including familiar faces from Stygian: Reign of the Old Ones.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44962233/fe3555956f9885e5c7543a9d2d17f719074be7bb.png[/img]

Naturally, iconic Lovecraftian characters, such as Keziah Mason, will make their presence felt, each woven into the eerie tapestry of the game, strengthening and expanding it with the threads of their own captivating storylines.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44962233/d9f6b72e5c98e55fa5e83f61922353c4a79fb670.png[/img]

Players will have the opportunity to not only meet familiar faces from the original Stygian, but also to discover iconic items; such as the H&W Military Police Revolver or the Cayuga Double-Barreled shotgun.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44962233/3e629b21812c0aa93a527b5a0a8661dc0242299a.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44962233/8450b32db263af9aff570d86d0092b728782735d.png[/img]

The game will feature a diverse arsenal of intriguing weapons, used in both ranged and melee combat - but don’t mistake it for a straightforward first-person shooter. Ammo will be scarce and enemies formidable - meaning that avoiding encounters through stealth might often be the wiser choice. “Choice” being a key word when talking about the gameplay in Stygian: Outer Gods, as the players will always have various options for how to approach an encounter. The game will also feature a character customization system that will let them unlock and upgrade skills and abilities to further hone their preferred playstyle – but more on that later, stay tuned!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44962233/b260e322d19ae2d0628466f1d191d6112a61cd10.png[/img]

We plan to gradually reveal more aspects of the game. After all, we haven’t yet touched on topics such as the immersive environment, role-playing elements, combat system, crafting, the protagonist’s supernatural abilities, survival mechanics, the role insanity will play, and more.

What would you like to hear about next? Write your questions in the comments - we’ll be sure to address the most popular and interesting ones in future developer diaries. And don’t forget to wishlist and follow the game here on Steam, so you don’t miss any of our coming updates!
